stories.name: Apple iPhone Duo launch
stories.blurb: Apple has unveiled its first foldable smartphone, the $1,999 iPhone Duo, marking its most expensive and dramatically redesigned iPhone yet.

stories.name: Vanguard Growth ETF Debate
stories.blurb: A recurring theme of financial articles comparing and recommending Vanguard growth-focused ETFs (like VUG and VGT) against rivals as long-term investment options.

stories.name: Apple CEO transition
stories.blurb: John Ternus succeeds Tim Cook as Apple CEO, raising questions about the company's future direction and leadership style.

stories.name: Apple Siri Smart Home Push
stories.blurb: Apple is launching a new Siri AI-powered smart home strategy centered on the HomeView hub and updated HomePod and Apple TV devices, alongside a broader Siri AI rollout.

stories.name: iPhone 18 production cuts
stories.blurb: Apple is cutting iPhone 18 Pro component orders and facing rising memory costs, pressuring its stock and pricing power.

stories.name: Apple Q3 earnings preview
stories.blurb: A cluster of headlines previewing Apple's upcoming third-quarter earnings report and debating whether the stock's record highs and rich valuation can be justified by results.

stories.name: Meta's Muse AI Surge
stories.blurb: Meta's stock rallies as its new AI app Muse gains rapid popularity, boosting investor confidence in the company's AI strategy ahead of Meta Connect.

stories.name: Tokenized Stock Trading
stories.blurb: Major financial and crypto firms are launching blockchain-based tokens of Apple, Nvidia, Tesla, and other U.S. stocks on Solana and other platforms, enabling 24/7 onchain trading of tokenized equities

stories.name: TSMC AI chip boom
stories.blurb: TSMC's surging AI chip demand and 2nm progress are driving record revenue and lifting Nvidia and other supplier stocks.

past.name: Apple Broadcom chip deal
past.blurb: Apple has signed a multi-year, $30 billion-plus agreement with Broadcom to supply chips through 2031, boosting Broadcom's stock and expanding its Colorado plant.

past.name: Qualcomm Apple patent deal
past.blurb: Qualcomm and Apple renewed their long-term global patent licensing agreement, easing investor fears about Qualcomm's revenue but leaving questions about its growth beyond Apple.

past.name: Iran-Israel Oil Market Swings
past.blurb: Stock markets fluctuate as investors react to escalating and de-escalating US-Iran/Middle East tensions, oil price swings, and their effects on earnings, Fed policy, and economic data.

past.name: Memory Chip Shortage
past.blurb: A global surge in memory and storage chip prices is forcing Apple to raise prices on MacBooks and iPads while even considering banned Chinese chip suppliers to cope with the shortage.

8.text: Apple’s first foldable iPhone, the $1,999–$2,000 iPhone Duo, went on sale Friday, October 23, with limited in-store supply after selling out in minutes and extended delivery waits. Early demand looked solid, including in China, though reviewers noted trade-offs and a $2,000 app problem.

5.text: Apple appears only as one of five mega-cap tech stocks driving concentration risk: it helps make up 30.8% of VOO and 49.2% of VUG, prompting recommendations for less concentrated alternatives. Other articles compare growth, dividend, and tech ETFs without materially focusing on Apple.

15.text: John Ternus became Apple CEO in September 2026 and may receive performance-based shares; Tim Cook stepped down after 15 years. Apple scheduled a launch event for new Pro Macs under Ternus, with AAPL around $343.

6.text: Apple unveiled a smart home lineup including HomeView, HomePod mini 2, and Home Collection, and is developing a higher-end HomeView with a robotic arm. It also announced an Oct. 28 event for a touchscreen MacBook Pro, expanded US suppliers, and faces UK and Polish regulatory pressure.

14.text: Analysts report weakening iPhone 18 Pro demand, citing shrinking lead times, falling resale prices, and order cuts. Loop Capital downgraded Apple to Hold, and UBS flagged slowing growth and margin pressure ahead of earnings.

7.text: Apple hit a new all-time high and is up 28% this year, outperforming the S&P 500 and the other Magnificent Seven stocks, though it fell 1% to $339.50 on Oct 20. Analysts debate its roughly 35x valuation, with some downgrading or calling it up to 25% overvalued ahead of earnings projected at $2 EPS.

11.text: Meta moved Q3 earnings up a week, beat revenue estimates at $64.6B, but shares fell on missed earnings and 2027 capex concerns; it paused Muse chat sharing after 6,800 exposed conversations. Meta's Muse agents aim to shop and run users' lives, potentially disrupting advertising and reducing reliance on Apple's platform terms.

16.text: Nine public companies objected to their shares being offered as blockchain-based tokens on a proposed OKX-ICE trading platform. Apple wasn't named among them, so the story bears on it only as a precedent for tokenized equities.

17.text: TSMC's Q3 revenue rose 41.2% and net income 68.7%, with high-performance computing now 68% of sales, driven by AI chip demand. Apple matters mainly as a major TSMC customer, though the articles focus on AI rather than Apple specifically.
